claims.summary: UPDATE modifies rows satisfying its predicate. The supplied current revision 42 passes >= 41, so this lower bound does not bind the payload to its source snapshot. A lower-bound test can serve a different range-selection task, but not equality with the captured generation revision.

Comparing the stored payload's revision 40 with the worker's 41 prevents some output regressions but ignores newer source revision 42. It would suffice only with an additional no-intervening-source-change guarantee, expressly contradicted by this fixture.

The application-supplied revision contract and ordinary UPDATE search condition allow the write only while source revision equals captured revision. This row fails 42=41, preserving its current state for a later retry. No native-vector, change-feed API or model return contract is claimed.

Nonnull presence is true for the stored revision-40 text payload and does not reject this race. It could restrict a job to already populated records, but cannot establish correspondence with the latest source revision.

An equality join returns each chunk with its one matching document, but it does not change the selected payload column. The fixture distinguishes whole-document and chunk-produced payloads. This selection could serve a design intentionally attaching document-level representations, not the required authoritative per-chunk output.

Selecting the chunk payload addresses representation identity, but CROSS JOIN still returns every document/chunk pair. That Cartesian relation can support a deliberate all-pairs analysis; it does not establish unique ownership in this multi-document batch.

Changing projected columns does not remove the cross-product rows. With at least two Documents, the same c tuple is returned multiple times. This could be harmless under a separately specified later deduplication or a single-document input, neither of which satisfies the stated exactly-one-row result here.

The FROM reference supplies the matching-pair semantics of an equality join; the given unique document key and valid chunk references yield one owner for every chunk. Selecting the supplied chunk-produced payload preserves the text/representation identity emphasized by the embedding-design training. All producer contracts are outside this fixed relational query.

The training pairs query and stored representations from the same model and explains that models determine their vector representations. Under the supplied immutable-S, full-capacity and paired-routing assumptions, retaining complete A/A until complete B/B is ready preserves both compatibility and coverage. No database snapshot or routing API is asserted.

Equal width is a supplied numeric property, not permission to ignore the explicitly rejected A/B comparisons. Immediate B queries could be valid if all served vectors were already B-compatible, but that is not the stated remaining A vector set.

The scenario explicitly says scale normalization did not establish cross-encoder compatibility. Normalization could be sufficient for a different problem involving only scale within a compatible representation, but it does not meet this supplied model-space contract.

Searching only converted rows can keep those individual comparisons within B's space, but drops part of the required immutable corpus S. Such a rollout could suit an offline or explicitly partial-coverage migration; neither is the service contract given here.
